newsitem.title: USA: Accuser says Army rigged hearing in McKinney's favor.
newsitem.headline: Accuser says Army rigged hearing in McKinney's favor.

text.p: Sgt. Maj. Brenda Hoster, the first woman to come forward with sexual harassment allegations against the Army's highest-ranking enlisted man, on Tuesday accused the military of rigging a pre-trial hearing in his favour.
Three other women soldiers have testified in an Army hearing to determine whether to court-martial Sergeant Major of the Army Gene McKinney, 46, but Hoster, who is retired, has refused to appear.

McKinney faces 18 charges including indecent assault, adultery and obstruction of justice in the latest of a series recent sex scandals that have rocked the U.S. armed services. He denies all the charges.

Hoster told ABC-TV's "Nightline" programme that the proceeding thus far had been "a free-for-all," citing tough cross-examination of McKinney's accusers, including one woman who said that she gave in to months of McKinney's advances and had unwanted sex with him on his couch while she was nearly eight months pregnant.
The woman was later asked if her husband was the baby's biological father.

Hoster said the other women were still in the military and had no choice but to testify, but she was a civilian and did not have to appear. "At least I can come forward and say this is not a fair and impartial hearing," she said.
Hoster also criticised a decision by Gen. Dennis Reimer, Army Chief of Staff, to testify as a character witness for McKinney, saying it amounted to "a slap in the face" for the victims.
"It's like saying he's a more important part of the team that they are now, and than I ever was," she told the ABC programme.

Hoster also denied allegations that have surfaced that she was gay and engaged in homosexual acts in her barracks. Another female soldier has made the allegations in a sworn affidavit given to McKinney's attorneys.
Hoster said she would only come to testify in the McKinney hearing if she received some assurance that her prior sexual history would not be discussed.
Army officials have threatened to recall Hoster back to active duty to force her to testify.
"I want to come and testify, but I am not going to come and testify until we play by the rules," Hoster said late on Tuesday in a television interview from Denver.
She said she would comply if she were ordered back to active duty.
